request.statement:
Generation Panels with Exclusive Selections

An administrator operates `N` image-generation panels, initially closed. Process `Q` events in order. Panel indices are `1..N`.

A panel stores whether it is open, its prompt, status, generated candidates, and selected candidates. Statuses are `IDLE`, `LOADING`, `READY`, `VALIDATION`, and `SERVICE`.

Input starts with `N Q`, followed by `Q` events:

- `OPEN i p`: discard all state of panel `i`, then open it with prompt `p` and status `IDLE`.
- `EDIT i p`: if `i` is open, replace its prompt; other state is unchanged.
- `START i`: every such event receives the next request number, starting at 1, even if it has no effect. If `i` is open, this becomes its sole pending request; set `LOADING` and discard candidates, selections, and errors. Its older requests become stale.
- `SUCCESS r k c1 ... ck`: if request `r` is the current pending request of its open panel, remove the pending request, set `READY`, and replace its candidates with the listed names, all unselected. Otherwise ignore it.
- `VALIDATION r e`: under the same acceptance condition, remove the pending request, discard candidates and selections, and set `VALIDATION` with error `e`.
- `SERVICE r e`: likewise, but set `SERVICE`.
- `TOGGLE i c`: if panel `i` is `READY` and contains candidate `c`, toggle that occurrence. If it changes from unselected to selected, any currently selected occurrence named `c` in any other panel is automatically deselected first. Thus, globally, at most one occurrence of each candidate name is selected. Otherwise do nothing.
- `CLOSE i`: discard all state of `i` and close it.
- `RESET l r`: simultaneously discard all state and close every panel from `l` through `r`; their requests become stale and their selections cease to exist.

Opening an open panel starts a fresh session. Editing does not stale a request. Each response names an earlier request, and each request has at most one response. Candidate names within one `SUCCESS` are distinct, but names may repeat between responses or panels.

Constraints: `1 <= N,Q <= 200000`; total `k` is at most `400000`; total token length is at most `4000000`. Prompts, candidate names, and errors are nonempty ASCII tokens without whitespace.

After all events, print one line per panel, in index order:

`i openness prompt status detail k candidate1 bit1 ... candidatek bitk`

A closed panel is `i CLOSED - IDLE - 0`. For an open panel, `detail` is the request number for `LOADING`, the error for `VALIDATION` or `SERVICE`, and `-` otherwise. Candidates are printed only for `READY`, in response order, with bit `1` if selected and `0` otherwise. Other statuses have `k = 0`.

Output is judged by splitting on ASCII whitespace and comparing tokens exactly.

Submit one complete Rust program using only the standard library and containing `fn main()`.
